question: What does polyvalent mean when describing a nurse?

options.A: Focused solely on community health education
options.B: Trained in multiple clinical skills and disciplines
options.C: Certified to practice medicine without supervision
options.D: Exclusively specialized in surgical theatre care

explanation: A polyvalent nurse has cross-training across fields like nursing, midwifery, and public health rather than just one narrow focus. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is polyvalent nursing important in the Nigerian healthcare system?

options.A: It helps combat severe staff shortages in rural health facilities
options.B: It eliminates the need for doctors in primary health centers
options.C: It allows nurses to prescribe any medication without restriction
options.D: It guarantees automatic promotion to senior management roles

explanation: Because remote areas lack specialized staff, multi-skilled nurses can handle diverse health needs ranging from general care to childbirth. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical duty of a polyvalent nurse?

options.C: Supervising junior healthcare staff and records
options.D: Managing acute clinical emergencies in rural clinics

explanation: Major specialized surgeries require a dedicated surgical team and are far beyond the scope of general polyvalent nursing practice. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient arrives at a remote primary health center in labor while the only doctor is away. What does the polyvalent nurse do?

options.A: Focus only on administrative paperwork while ignoring the laboring mother
options.B: Use multi-skilled training to safely manage the delivery and monitor the mother
options.C: Wait for specialized obstetricians to arrive before touching the patient
options.D: Refer the patient immediately without any examination due to lack of a doctor

explanation: Because polyvalent nurses are cross-trained in midwifery, they can manage normal deliveries when specialized personnel are absent. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h2)

question: How does a polyvalent nurse support primary healthcare centers in Nigeria?

options.A: By lobbying the federal government for increased health budgets
options.B: By performing multiple distinct health roles to make up for staff shortages
options.C: By replacing traditional birth attendants with modern machinery
options.D: By restricting clinic access to only severe medical emergencies

explanation: Polyvalent nurses bridge gaps by handling various duties, ensuring that patients receive comprehensive care despite a lack of specialized staff. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary foundation of health promotion and disease prevention in Nigeria?
explanation: Primary healthcare is the first level of contact individuals have with the national health system, focusing on community-level promotion and prevention. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why is mental flexibility and adaptability important for a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: They rarely work with patients and spend most of their time doing research
options.B: They must change their professional title depending on who is visiting
options.C: They are required to rotate to a new hospital department every single day
options.D: They must rapidly switch between very different clinical duties and environments

explanation: Moving from emergency trauma care to maternal health or community outreach requires quick mental shifts and broad clinical readiness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h4)

question: What should a polyvalent nurse do when basic diagnostic resources are missing in a clinic?

options.A: Close down the entire facility until new equipment is delivered
options.B: Ignore the patient's symptoms until they can afford private tests
options.C: Blame the patients for coming to an under-equipped health center
options.D: Innovate safely to manage care without compromising professional standards

explanation: Resource scarcity is common in rural settings, requiring nurses to use clinical judgment and safe improvisation to help patients. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge faced by polyvalent nurses?

options.A: High risk of burnout due to heavy and diverse workloads
options.B: Guaranteed high salaries that exceed medical doctors
options.C: Excessive free time and lack of meaningful clinical tasks
options.D: Automatic exemption from all night-shift duties

explanation: Managing multiple roles across different specialties with limited staff often leads to physical and emotional exhaustion. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is meant by professional ambiguity in generalist nursing?

options.A: Not knowing whether one is a registered nurse or a pharmacist
options.B: Confusion over which language to speak with foreign patients
options.C: Unclear boundaries between tasks meant for different specialties
options.D: The inability to remember basic vital sign measurements

explanation: Because polyvalent nurses cross traditional professional borders, overlapping roles can sometimes cause confusion in multidisciplinary teams. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h5)
